400°F The cut depends on the food, so one number is never the whole answer. Each cell gives the air fryer temperature, °C, gas mark and the share of the oven time you save. Food Basket Oven-style General / mixed 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time Fries & potatoes 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 30% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 25% less time Chicken wings 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time Chicken breast (boneless) 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 25% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time Chicken thighs / bone-in 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time Steak & thick cuts 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time 385°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time Fish & salmon 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time 385°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time Bacon 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 30% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 25% less time Vegetables 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 25% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time Baked goods & cookies 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time 385°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 10% less time Pizza & reheating 375°F / 190°C Gas mark 5 · 25% less time 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 20% less time Casseroles & thick bakes 380°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 15% less time 385°F / 195°C Gas mark 5 · 10% less time What recipes use 400°F 400°F (205°C, gas mark 6) is the classic roasting setting. Recipes use it for vegetables, potato wedges, chicken breast, sausages, salmon fillets, roasted chickpeas, homemade fries and anything finished with a crisp edge. An air fryer is a roaster at heart, so this is where it most clearly beats the oven: a general recipe drops to 375°F, and fries take the largest time cut in the table, with roast vegetables close behind, because they have lots of surface and little depth. Notice that the conversion never asks the basket to reach 400°F itself. The air fryer gets the same browning about 20% faster at a lower setting, which leaves headroom below the 400°F maximum most basket units have. The failure mode at 400°F: steamed, not roasted High heat in a small space only works if the moisture can get away. Cut vegetables and potatoes release water as they heat, and in a full basket that steam stays around the food, so instead of browning it softens and goes pale. It is the most common complaint about air-fried vegetables, and more time does not fix it. Cook in a single layer with gaps, or in two batches; the second batch is usually a minute or two faster because the basket is already hot. Dry vegetables well after washing, toss them in a teaspoon of oil rather than a spoonful, and shake the basket at the check time so the pieces at the bottom come up into the air. Fat dripping from sausages or chicken skin can smoke at this heat, so empty the drawer between batches. Worked example A recipe roasts mixed vegetables at 400°F for 25 minutes. A basket air fryer does it at 375°F (190°C) in 19 minutes, with a shake at 13 minutes to check the colour. An oven-style air fryer takes 380°F for 20 minutes; spread the vegetables over two racks rather than piling one, and swap the racks halfway. 400°F to °C in an air fryer The exact conversion of 400°F is 204°C, rounded here to 205°C, while European recipes and oven dials usually round it to 200°C. That small gap does not matter in a roast. What matters is that the air fryer setting is lower: 190°C in a basket unit, 195°C in an oven-style one. If your air fryer only moves in 10°C steps, pick the lower step for potatoes and vegetables, which brown well anyway, and the higher one for chicken skin. Entering the recipe in °C in the converter gives you both numbers at once. Nearby temperatures 375°F oven to air fryer → 425°F oven to air fryer → Oven to air fryer converter (any temperature) → Printable conversion chart → Frozen food mode (packaging instructions) → Frequently asked questions What is 400°F in an air fryer? About 375°F (190°C) in a basket air fryer, with about 20% less time. In an oven-style unit, 380°F. Fries and bacon save the most time; baked goods and casseroles take the smallest cut. 400°F to °C: what do I set on my air fryer? The recipe temperature is 205°C, often printed as 200°C. Set a basket air fryer to 190°C or an oven-style one to 195°C, and cut the time by roughly 20%. Can my air fryer go to 400°F? Most basket units reach 400°F and oven-style units 450°F, so yes, but you rarely need to. A 400°F oven recipe converts to a lower setting because the air fryer browns faster; set 400°F only when an air fryer recipe itself asks for it. How long do roast potatoes take in the air fryer from a 400°F recipe? Roughly a quarter less than the oven time for cut potatoes and other vegetables, at 375°F. Chunks cook faster than small whole potatoes. Shake twice, and judge by colour and a knife through the thickest piece. Why are my air fryer vegetables soggy at 375°F? Almost always overcrowding. The steam from the vegetables cannot escape, so they cook in it. Use a single layer, dry them well and use less oil; a hotter setting will not rescue a full basket.
